Proposition 1 (Orthonormal Grassmann Col.claim: For any orthonormal frame Q in R^{k x 8} (Q Q^T = I_k), G = I_k and R = G * G = I_k. The relational matrix is identically the identity across all orthonormal frames in Gr(k, 8).

Proposition 2 (Subspace Blindness on Gra.claim: For any two distinct orthonormal subspaces S_1, S_2 in Gr(k, 8), R_1 = R_2 = I_k. G2 explicit geometric bias cannot distinguish orthonormal subspaces.

Proposition 3 (Rank-1 Inefficacy of G2).claim: For k=1, R = [1.0]. Softmax over a singleton token is identically [1.0] for all beta. G2 has zero influence on rank-1 inference.

Proposition 4 (Equivalence to Diagonal C.claim: Under orthonormal frames, G2 is functionally identical to adding learned scalar beta to self-attention logits (control_diagonal_bias).

Proposition 5 (Non-orthogonal Divergence.claim: When operators are non-orthogonal (e.g. redundant limb leads), G2 off-diagonal R_ij terms become active, producing distinct outputs from diagonal control.

Proposition 6 (Higher-Order Redundancy L.claim: Two valid Gram matrices G_A (coplanar, 120-degree unit vectors, rank 2, linearly dependent) and G_B (equilateral spherical triangle, rank 3, linearly independent) produce bitwise identical squared relational matrices R_A = R_B = [[1, 1/4, 1/4], [1/4, 1, 1/4], [1/4, 1/4, 1]]. G2 squared Gram features cannot determine measurement subspace rank or distinguish higher-order linear dependence.
